subject: armadillo
pitch: A nine-banded armadillo trotting along. A shell of overlapping banded plates in dusty pinkish-tan, a pointy snout, tall leathery ears, small beady eyes, sturdy clawed feet and a long armoured tail tapering to a point. A sprinkle of coarse pale hairs pokes out between the bands.
reasoning:
I'm planning the armadillo's overall proportions and a neutral standing pose, then sketching out the skeleton hierarchy starting with the pelvis as the root joint for the spine chain.

From there I'm mapping out each joint's position: spine, chest, neck, head, and jaw, followed by a tail built as a chain of joints running backward and downward, which I'll render as a smooth tapered sweep. Next I'm working out how to construct the shell of the body using bands.

Building shell bands...

Legs add about 0.06 to the height, keeping total near 0.23, with the dome only covering the upper shell since the belly hides the lower half. For the band segments I'm using rotated, non-uniformly scaled cylinders so each one stretches to match the body's width and height profile along its length, using a low-poly radial segment count for a faceted look.

For coloring, I'm alternating slightly different band colors toward the back and using a paint function that checks local y-position to switch between a pale belly tone and the main shell colors, avoiding messy half-cylinder geometry tricks.

I'll avoid that conflict and define my own mix helper, importing paint and smoothstep as needed. For texture, I'm adding a scales paint pattern on the shield areas for the shoulders and pelvis, then shaping the head as a wedge with a pointed snout using a scaled sphere plus a forward-aimed cone geometry.

Now I'm detailing facial features: a smaller pale cone for the lower jaw, a tiny dark pink sphere for the nose tip, small black eye spheres with highlights, and tall thin leathery cone-shaped ears tilted outward with darker pink inner coloring, plus a scaled shell-like plate covering the top of the head.

Then I'm working out the leg structure: front and hind leg positions with a joint chain from hip to knee to ankle to paw, built from skin-colored capsule sweeps weighted to bones, finishing with clawed cones on the paws, longer in front.

Now I'm planning the hairy fringe between the body's color bands - small spike-like cones placed in tufts along both sides where the body width is widest, keeping the total part count well under budget.

I'm also working out the body's shape math, defining a width/height function based on z-position so the shell narrows toward the head and tail, then spacing the color bands (front shield, nine middle bands, pelvic shield) so they overlap slightly without gaps. Underneath the shell I'm adding a slightly smaller pale-colored core ellipsoid to suggest the belly peeking through.

For the tail, I'm sweeping a tapering radius along a curved path made of a few control points, painting it with darker stripe bands, and considering adding small torus rings along the tail for extra ridge detail, though stripes alone might already do the job.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: a pelvis root joint, spine1 and spine2 above it, then neck, head, and jaw joints continuing forward along the z-axis, each parented to the previous one so the whole chain inherits orientation naturally.

Setting up manual joints instead for simplicity, since chain roles seem more trouble than they're worth here. I'll just define joints directly rather than fight with the chain/polyline helper for neck and spine.

For ears, I'm defining the joint positions and using a flattened cone geometry (4-sided, scaled thin) positioned at the joint and translated so its base sits at the joint origin, oriented along the ear's direction vector.

With 4 radial segments the cone's cross-section forms a diamond shape with tips along x and z, so scaling z down to 0.3 makes a wide, thin flap aligned correctly for an ear using default roll orientation. I'll add a smaller pink inner-ear layer offset slightly forward, set the left/right ears apart with outward tilt, and now I'm choosing the color palette—pinkish-tan shell tones and a lighter belly color.

Now I'm defining the eyes as tiny black spheres with white highlights positioned on the head, then building the skull as a scaled ellipsoid and the snout as a small low-poly cone tapering toward the nose tip.

Still shaping the head...

Now I'm working out the paw geometry so the toes touch the ground without clipping below zero, then laying out the front leg joint positions from hip to toe tip before moving on to the hind legs.

Checking that the hind leg joints form a more bent pose than the front, with the knee pulled forward and the hip tucked inside the body's cross-section so the legs appear to emerge naturally beneath the shell. Now I'm adding small claw cones to each foot.

Still writing leg capsules...

For other joints I'll aim bones toward the next joint so they orient correctly, like aiming the paw bone at the toe. For the tail, I'm tapering the ring radius along its length and using a thin torus tube for each segment.

Now I'm placing hair spikes at the rear edges of each band, pointing outward with a normal direction and slight downward tilt, using cones scaled to sit just inside the surface -- about six hairs per band across both sides.

I'm also setting up band shading logic, darkening the rear edge of each band toward a reddish-brown tone using a smoothstep gradient based on z-position, while keeping the belly a separate flat color.

Setting up scale paint textures...

Adding dome spheres for the front shield and rear pelvic areas, computing their tapered widths based on the ellipse profile, then moving into writing the actual part-generation code.

Now I'm sketching out the tail as a chained sequence of torus-ring segments following a Catmull-Rom spline, orienting each ring's axis along the tangent direction, with striped coloring along the sweep.
